A1.justification: Both PDFs, including their appendices, are readable and describe the same Mamba pruning study. Matching methods and benchmark tables establish correspondence despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original language-modeling, forecasting, classification, efficiency, robustness and ablation results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark results and adds compression comparisons, architecture comparisons and mechanism analyses.

M1.justification: Beyond v1's gradient-magnitude scoring, global masking and corrective stability checks, v2 introduces gating-diversity weighting, interaction-graph centrality weighting, and eigenvalue-penalized fine-tuning with variable stabilization duration. Sections 3.3 and D.8 describe substantive changes to scoring and optimization.

E1.justification: The core datasets and domains remain, including the audio and vision evaluations matched between v1 Table 12 and v2 Table 11. However, explicit paraphrase and mixed-perturbation evaluation scenarios from v1 Table 14 disappear.

E2.justification: v2 Table 9 adds evaluated SNIP, Movement Pruning, Wanda, GraSP, structured pruning and Lottery Ticket comparisons. Appendix F adds quantization and hybrid compression comparisons. Cross-architecture comparisons expand to efficient Transformers and hybrid models, while the earlier explicit LSTM comparison disappears.

E3.justification: New evaluations specify channel-wise L1 pruning, symmetric 8-bit quantization excluding layer normalization, and hybrid compression protocols. Mechanism studies introduce training-validation comparisons, gating analysis over 1,000 inputs and loss-landscape measurements. The earlier V100 and Jetson evaluation settings disappear; principal benchmark settings largely persist.

E4.justification: v2 adds generalization-gap, gating-stability, loss-landscape and new-component ablations, and expands architecture-transfer analysis. Earlier detailed component ablations, intermediate gradient-exponent tests and extended perturbation tables are removed or reduced. The existing stability-threshold analysis is retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests. v2's gating standard-deviation measurement describes activation variability, rather than uncertainty in benchmark estimates.

E6.justification: Tables 1–7 and the matched cross-dataset table retain their reported numbers. v2 adds comparator scores, compression results and quantitative mechanism findings, including a 14.3% smaller generalization gap. Several earlier ablation, perturbation and hardware entries disappear. New Figure 9 reports linear/exponential endpoints of 21.0/20.9, conflicting with Table 8's retained 21.4/21.1.

T1.justification: The original eigenvalue-shift inequality is retained and repeated in the main text. Appendix D.9 adds input-dependent transition definitions, sensitivity coefficients, Theorem 1 and a stability-constrained optimization formulation. It also asserts an approximation guarantee and proofs without supplying those proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction qualify the headline performance claim from over 95% retention to 3–9% loss, while retaining the 70% parameter-reduction claim and contribution list. The conclusion still claims over 95% retention, leaving the qualification inconsistent.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands explanations involving gating stability, intrinsic dimensionality, loss landscapes and compression trade-offs. It adds dataset-bias and energy considerations and a limitation to models up to 370M parameters, although Figure 5 labels a 1.4B model. Several interpretations become stronger causal assertions than v1's hypotheses.

D1.justification: Most existing hyperparameters are consolidated in Table 10. v2 newly reports 72/180-hour training times, COO storage and profiling details, quantization implementation information and release plans upon acceptance. v1's model depths and hidden dimensions disappear, and the code URL remains redacted.

R1.justification: v2 broadens positioning against modern pruning and quantization methods, efficient Transformers and hybrid architectures. It adds connections to intrinsic-dimension and loss-landscape research and more explicit distinctions from standard pruning. Several dataset and architecture references accompanying v1's experimental setup are removed.

P1.justification: The narrative is substantially reorganized: theoretical material enters the main methodology, robustness moves into a separate comparative-analysis section, limitations and future work become separate sections, and appendices are restructured. The abstract and many captions are rewritten, with substantially expanded explanatory passages.

P2.justification: v2 switches to a two-column layout, adds a workflow diagram and numerous analysis plots, and redraws or expands importance, allocation and architecture figures. Earlier ablation tables are consolidated, several supplementary tables disappear, and retained figures and tables are extensively resized and relocated.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful comparison coverage, mechanism analyses and more explicit limitations, but removes detailed ablations and hardware measurements. It also introduces reliability problems: Section 5.3 incorrectly ranks Wanda above magnitude pruning despite perplexities of 21.9 versus 21.5; Section 4.5's COO calculation evaluates to 6N rather than 1.8N; and Appendix D.9 asserts proofs without presenting them. These substantive benefits and harms prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
